text: A central advantage claimed for teleological (biosemantic) theories of content, such as Millikan's, over pure informational theories is that they:
choices: Reduce all mental content to conscious experience
Avoid any appeal to evolutionary history
Explain misrepresentation — why a frog's fly-detector tokened by a passing BB pellet counts as an error, a misfiring of what the state is for
Show that meaning is entirely in the head
explanation: Teleological theories fix content by a state's biological function — what it was selected to indicate — so a detector triggered by a BB pellet misrepresents, because BB pellets are not what it is for. Pure informational (covariation) theories struggle here (the disjunction problem). Option 1 is false (teleosemantics centrally uses evolutionary history); options 0 and 3 misdescribe the view.
